scope: Proposition 4.1 (Uniform one-site closure) of the manuscript “The low-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick fluctuation scale” (preprints/The-low-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-fluctuation-scale-September-24-2026/The-low-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-fluctuation-scale-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 217 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e0e2e5e34169e701), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 33. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix 0 < c < C < ∞. At a target cut i satisfying ri ≤ Cx and cx ≤ ui ≤ Cx, along every sequence with Di = o(x), Si = Γ(Ki) + o(x3 ). (22) The bound is O(x3), uniformly over these targets, if Di = O(x). More precisely, for a fixed direct-test sequence there are ηn → 0, C0 < ∞, and ϑ > 0, independent of the target in this band, such that |Si − Γ(Ki)| x3 ≤ C0{ηn + (Di/x)ϑ }. When W = O(x), the O(x3) assertion also holds at every omitted lower cut, without a lower bound on its mass and without (4) at that cut. On the bands in (19), the error in (22), divided by x3, tends to zero in normalized L1, in both mass and radius coordinates.
